chapters.n: This is likely Paul’s last surviving letter, written from a Roman prison shortly before his execution. He is an apostle sent to proclaim the promise of life in Christ.
Paul addresses Timothy tenderly as his “dearly beloved son,” with grace, mercy, and peace.
Paul serves God with a clear conscience, as his ancestors did, and he prays for Timothy constantly, night and day.

f.g: In continuity with his faithful Jewish ancestors.

chapters.n: Remembering Timothy’s tears at their last parting, Paul longs to see him so his joy can be complete.
Paul recalls Timothy’s sincere faith, which first lived in his grandmother Lois and mother Eunice. Faith passed through generations of faithful women.
So Paul reminds Timothy to fan into flame the gift God gave him when Paul laid his hands on him. Spiritual gifts must be actively kindled.
God did not give us a spirit of timidity, but of power, love, and self-discipline.
So don’t be ashamed to testify of the Lord, or of Paul, His prisoner. Share in suffering for the gospel, relying on God’s power.
God saved us and called us to a holy life — not because of our works, but because of His own purpose and grace, given to us in Christ before the world began.
That grace has now been revealed through Christ’s coming. He destroyed death’s power and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.
For this gospel Paul was appointed a preacher, apostle, and teacher.
That’s why Paul suffers, but he isn’t ashamed. He knows the One he has trusted and is sure Christ can guard what Paul has entrusted to Him until the Judgment Day.

f.w: I know whom I have believed
that which I have committed unto him
f.g: What Paul deposited with Christ — his life and soul.
The day of judgment and Christ’s return.

chapters.n: Keep following the pattern of healthy teaching you learned from me, with faith and love in Christ.
Guard the precious truth entrusted to you, with the help of the Holy Ghost who lives in us.

f.w: That good thing which was committed unto thee

chapters.n: Sadly, nearly everyone in the province of Asia has deserted Paul, including Phygellus and Hermogenes.

f.g: The Roman province in western Turkey, capital Ephesus.

chapters.n: May the Lord bless the family of Onesiphorus, who often encouraged Paul and wasn’t embarrassed by his chains.
When he came to Rome, he searched hard until he found Paul — no small effort in a huge city, for an imprisoned man.
Paul prays the Lord will show him mercy on Judgment Day. Timothy knows well how much he helped in Ephesus too.
So, my son, be strong through the grace that is found in Christ — strength not from yourself but from Him.
Pass on what you heard from me to trustworthy people who can teach others. Paul pictures four generations: Paul, Timothy, faithful men, and others.
Endure hardship like a good soldier of Christ. Paul begins three images: soldier, athlete, farmer.
A soldier on duty doesn’t get tangled up in civilian business; he aims to please his commander.
An athlete doesn’t win the victor’s crown unless he competes by the rules.
The hardworking farmer should be the first to enjoy the harvest. Faithful labor brings its reward.
Think about these illustrations, and the Lord will help you understand.
Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David. These two truths — His divine victory and His royal human lineage — are at the heart of Paul’s gospel.
For this gospel Paul is chained like a criminal — but God’s word can’t be chained.

f.w: the word of God is not bound

chapters.n: So Paul endures everything for the sake of God’s chosen people, that they too may receive salvation in Christ and eternal glory.

f.g: For the sake of God’s chosen ones.

chapters.n: A trustworthy saying, possibly an early hymn: if we have died with Christ, we will also live with Him.
If we endure, we will reign with Him; if we deny Him, He will deny us.
Even when we are faithless, He remains faithful — He cannot be untrue to Himself. Christ’s reliability does not depend on ours.
Keep reminding the members of these truths, and warn them before God not to fight over words. It does no good and only ruins those listening.
Work hard to present yourself to God as an approved worker who has no reason for shame, correctly handling the word of truth.

f.g: Cutting straight — handling correctly, like cutting a straight path.

chapters.n: Avoid irreverent, empty chatter; it only leads to more ungodliness.
Such talk spreads like gangrene. Hymenaeus and Philetus are examples.
They have abandoned the truth by claiming the resurrection has already happened — probably as a purely spiritual event — and are upsetting some people’s faith.
Still, God’s firm foundation stands, sealed with two inscriptions: “The Lord knows those who are His” and “Everyone who calls on Christ’s name must turn from evil.”

f.w: The Lord knoweth them that are his

chapters.n: In a large house there are fine dishes of gold and silver and plain ones of wood and clay — some for honored use, some for common use.
If someone cleanses himself from what is dishonorable, he becomes a vessel for honor — holy, useful to the Master, and ready for every good work.
Flee the desires typical of youth, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace together with others who call on the Lord with a pure heart.

f.g: Desires and impulses typical of youth, including impatience and pride as well as passion.

chapters.n: Steer clear of foolish, ignorant debates; they only breed quarrels.
The Lord’s servant must not be quarrelsome but kind to everyone, able to teach, and patient when wronged.
Gently teach those who oppose you. Perhaps God will grant them repentance and lead them to know the truth.
Then they may come to their senses and escape the devil’s trap, after being held captive by him to do his will.

f.g: Come back to their senses, sober up.

chapters.n: Understand this: in the last days there will be dangerous, difficult times. Latter-day Saints often read this list as a description of our own day.
People will be self-centered, greedy, boastful, arrogant, abusive, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, and unholy.
They will be heartless, unwilling to make peace, slanderers, without self-control, brutal, and hostile to anything good.

f.g: Lacking normal love even for family.

chapters.n: They will be treacherous, reckless, conceited, loving pleasure rather than God.

f.w: lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God

chapters.n: They will keep an outward show of religion but reject its real power to change lives. Stay away from such people. Joseph Smith heard similar words in the First Vision.
Some of them worm their way into homes and gain control over vulnerable people weighed down with sins and swayed by many desires.

f.g: Greek gynaikaria — weak or vulnerable people (literally “little women”), easily misled.

chapters.n: These people are always learning but never arrive at real knowledge of the truth. Information without humility does not lead to truth.
Just as Jannes and Jambres — names Jewish tradition gave to Pharaoh’s magicians — opposed Moses, these false teachers oppose the truth. Their minds are corrupt and their faith counterfeit.

f.g: Not named in Exodus; the names come from Jewish tradition.

chapters.n: But they won’t get very far; their foolishness will become obvious to everyone, as happened with Pharaoh’s magicians.
By contrast, Timothy has closely followed Paul’s teaching, way of life, purpose, faith, patience, love, and endurance.
He also knows the persecutions Paul suffered in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra — near Timothy’s hometown — and how the Lord rescued him from them all.
In fact, everyone who wants to live a godly life in Christ will face persecution.
Evil people and impostors will go from bad to worse, deceiving others and being deceived themselves.
But you, Timothy, hold on to what you have learned and become convinced of, remembering the trustworthy people who taught you.

f.w: of whom thou hast learned them

chapters.n: From childhood you have known the holy scriptures — the Old Testament — which can make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ.

f.g: The Hebrew scriptures, our Old Testament.

chapters.n: All scripture is inspired by God and useful for teaching truth, correcting error, setting things right, and training in righteous living.
Scripture equips God’s servant to be complete and fully prepared for every good work.
Paul gives his solemn final charge before God and Christ, who will judge the living and the dead when He appears and establishes His kingdom.
Preach the word. Be ready whether the time seems convenient or not. Correct, warn, and encourage with great patience and careful teaching.

f.g: Be ready, stand by, be on duty.

chapters.n: A time is coming when people won’t tolerate healthy teaching. Instead, to suit their own desires, they will collect teachers who tell them what their itching ears want to hear.

f.g: Ears eager for novel, pleasing ideas.

chapters.n: They will turn away from the truth and wander off into myths.
But you, Timothy, keep your head in all situations, endure hardship, do the work of spreading the gospel, and fully carry out your ministry.

f.g: One who proclaims the good news.

chapters.n: Paul knows his death is near. His life is already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time has come for his departure.

f.g: Poured out as a drink offering.
Greek analysis — loosing a ship from its moorings or striking a tent.

chapters.n: Paul’s famous summary of his life: I have fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith.

f.w: I have fought a good fight

chapters.n: Now a victor’s crown of righteousness awaits him, which the Lord, the just Judge, will give him on that day — and not only him, but everyone who longs for Christ’s appearing.

f.g: Who long for and look forward to His coming.

chapters.n: Paul urges Timothy to come quickly.
Demas has abandoned Paul because he loved this present world and went to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus to Dalmatia.

f.g: A region on the Adriatic coast, roughly modern Croatia.

chapters.n: Only Luke is with Paul. Bring Mark, he says, for he is useful in the ministry — a moving reconciliation with the young man who once left Paul’s mission.
Paul has sent Tychicus to Ephesus — possibly to relieve Timothy so he can come.
Bring my cloak that I left in Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments. Facing a cold cell and death, Paul still wants his warm cloak and his books — likely scripture.

f.g: Writings on leather, perhaps scriptures or personal records.

chapters.n: Alexander the metalworker did Paul great harm. Paul leaves judgment to the Lord, who will repay him for what he has done.
Paul warns Timothy to be on guard against him, because he strongly opposed their message.
At Paul’s first court hearing, no one stood by him — everyone deserted him. Like Jesus and Stephen, he prays it won’t be held against them.

f.w: not be laid to their charge

chapters.n: But the Lord stood by him and gave him strength, so the gospel was fully proclaimed for Gentiles to hear. He was rescued “from the lion’s mouth” — from mortal danger.
Paul trusts the Lord will rescue him from every evil and bring him safely into His heavenly kingdom — even if that rescue comes through death.

f.w: preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom

chapters.n: Paul sends greetings to Prisca (Priscilla) and Aquila, his longtime friends and fellow tentmakers, and to Onesiphorus’s household.
Erastus stayed in Corinth, and Paul left Trophimus sick in Miletus. Even Paul could not always heal his companions.
Come before winter, Paul pleads — sailing stopped in winter, and he may not have much longer. Several Roman Saints send their greetings.

f.g: Early tradition names a Linus as a leader of the Church in Rome.

chapters.n: Paul’s last recorded words: the Lord be with your spirit; grace be with you all.

f.g: The “you” here is plural — a blessing on the whole Church.
